documents.summary: UVM's Code of Academic Integrity is a general conduct code, and its one AI-specific line sits inside the cheating standard. Work generated by AI is not counted as the student's own and is not permitted unless the instructor expressly says so. The rest of the code is process: who reports, how hearings work, sanctions.
documents.stance_why: The cheating standard says 'Work generated by artificial intelligence is not considered to be created by the student and is not permitted unless expressly stated by the instructor.' AI is banned by default and allowed only where an instructor says so, which is restrict. It does not delegate the default to instructors, because the ban applies unless an exception is stated.

P81 fits because it is a required reporting step with a deadline.

notes: Four UVM documents were coded (Code of Academic Integrity, About AI at UVM, WID 'Teaching and Writing in the Age of AI', Writing Centers GenAI guide); no school or computing-unit policy was found, and the AI-site sub-pages and the CS1210 syllabus were not coded (empty shells or deferred). The Code has one AI sentence ('Work generated by artificial intelligence is not considered to be created by the student and is not permitted unless expressly stated by the instructor'), so the Code is coded as restrict. The general hearing, appeal and mitigation provisions (coder A units on council meetings, standard of proof, technical violation, reflective essay, alternative resolution) were dropped as unrelated to AI; reporting, the faculty's role in sanctions, and the first-offence XF were kept because they are how AI cheating is processed. The WID page quotes sample statements from UMass Amherst, Cumming, Texas Tech, UPenn, UC Irvine and Illinois State alongside UVM Center for Student Conduct language; they are coded as the UVM page's model language and the tiers list follows its five headings. Repeated sentences in the samples ('Violations could result in failure...') are coded once. Candidate new types: (1) require the instructor's prior permission before any AI use (UNCOVERED, WID UVM and UPenn samples; coder A, with coder B using P10 and a fit_note); (2) decide whether policy separates AI assistance from AI text generation (UNCOVERED, WID reflection question; also partial fits in P09 and P15 units).
